messages:
Alex P: Hey team — FinBank pilot reporting missing trace IDs in their logs after routing through our gateway. Also seeing intermittent 429s. Can we swarm? I flagged their account: account-id=finbank-03.
Joe - Sales: On it. Looping in SEs and infra. Who can take initial log/trace check? :wave:
Rebecca (SE): I can start. Quick Q: are they on Private or Hosted? Trace propagation differs if they have an edge proxy.
Alex P: Hosted (trial shard us-west-2), but they front with an nginx reverse proxy in their VPC.
Maria L: I see spikes from that tenant around 11:06 UTC -> autoscaler lagged. Also noticed their requests arrive without `traceparent` or `x-request-id` headers at our ingress. Sample snippet from gateway logs:
```
2026-03-20T11:06:12Z INFO req_id= - path=/v1/generate status=200 latency=12ms
2026-03-20T11:06:12Z INFO req_id= - path=/v1/generate status=429 latency=3ms
```
No trace ids attached.
Samir: If nginx strips headers by default you need to forward the trace header. Typical fix in nginx: `proxy_set_header Traceparent $http_traceparent; proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;`
Rebecca (SE): Can someone paste a minimal curl repro we can ask the customer to run? If we can reproduce we can rule out our side.
Maria L: Repro curl I used against the gateway (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' -v
```
When sent with `traceparent` we see `trace_id=4bf92f3577b34da6` in our logs. Without it, `req_id` is empty.
Joe - Sales: Customer also asked about exporting logs to Splunk / Datadog and whether trace IDs will flow through those exports.
Maria L: Yes — for hosted customers, trace ids are included in the structured log payload if present. For log drains, set `trace_id_key` in the sink config. Example drain config we provide: 
```
{
  "type": "datadog",
  "endpoint": "https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input",
  "api_key": "<redacted>",
  "trace_id_key": "trace_id",
  "sample_rate": 1.0
}
```
Rebecca (SE): Security question: does this require KMS/HSM changes? Short answer: no for trace propagation; those headers are ephemeral. For Private deployments customers can opt into KMS for stored logs. I'll answer their questionnaire with that.
Infra Bot: autoscaler: scaled finbank-03 gateway 1 -> 4 replicas in 46s (reason: CPU spike)
Samir: Another gotcha — some client libraries send `traceparent` in lowercase or as `Traceparent`. Upstream proxies sometimes normalize headers; ensure nginx config preserves them. If they're on older AWS ALB they need `proxy_pass_request_headers on;`
Alex P: Rebecca — can you draft the sec answer and I'll send to customer? Also can someone join a quick troubleshooting call at 11:30 PT?
Rebecca (SE): I'll draft. I can join 11:30 PT. :thumbsup:
Maria L: I'll join too. I'll ask infra to grab the customer's nginx config (they said they can share sanitized config).
Joe - Sales: I'll coordinate the invite and add the CISO contact for the questionnaire follow-up.
Alex P: Thanks all — I'll update the customer: ask them to run the curl with `traceparent` and to check their nginx for header forwarding. Will follow up after the 11:30 call. :pray:
